entry_state: Rate bounds preserve a shared loan history and cannot be mixed into journals. Contract modification and credit reassessment are separate; equal terminal wealth can hide a wrong interest basis. Legal release and asset-transfer conditions require their own evidence.
exit_state: Late collateral receipts belong in loss measurement and do not become a separately owned asset. Revolving capacity preserves credit history; fee purpose determines yield or service timing. Partial transfer now requires identifying the eligible asset portion.
findings: The collateral example changes to a half-year factor of 1.1 explicitly. Omitting later collateral would give loss 40 instead of 20.
Enforcement costs are included once; final cash 166.55 and equity negative 13.45 reconcile the 33.45 loss. Financial write-off does not waive the legal claim.
Revolving capacity after draw, repayment and redraw is 50; loss balances total 5.2 and equity 14.8. The mechanical capacity path does not calibrate a loss horizon.
Fee receipt alone is neither service revenue nor evidence of zero credit risk. The separate yield example's 9.8 equals net cash. No new defect observed.
